practice.question: Explain what happens when a species has an unpaired electron: how it forms, how reactive it is and what usually becomes of it.
practice.answer: It is a radical: formed by homolytic fission of a covalent bond, highly reactive, short-lived (an intermediate) that quickly reacts with another radical to make a new covalent compound.
steps: An unpaired electron makes the species a radical.
Radicals form when a shared pair splits evenly, one electron to each atom.
They are very reactive and short-lived, so they act as intermediates.
They combine with other radicals to give new covalently bonded molecules.

practice.question: Which of these is a propagation step in the radical substitution of ethane by chlorine?
steps: A propagation step has one radical and one non-radical reactant, giving one radical and one non-radical product.
A is initiation; C is termination (two radicals, no radical product).
D is not a valid step: it gives an H radical and C2H5Cl, which is not how the chain proceeds.
B regenerates Cl•, so the chain continues.

practice.question: Methane and chlorine react in sunlight: CH4(g) + Cl2(g) → CH3Cl(g) + HCl(g). What type of reaction is this?
steps: Sunlight (UV) splits Cl2 into radicals.
One H is replaced by Cl, so it is substitution via radicals.

practice.question: Which reaction goes by a radical mechanism when UV light is present?
steps: Alkane halogenation under UV light is radical substitution.
A is electrophilic substitution of benzene, B is hydrogenation, C is electrophilic addition to an alkene.

practice.question: Define homolytic fission and state the conditions needed for it to occur. [2]
practice.answer: The two bonding electrons of a covalent bond are shared out evenly between the two atoms, giving two radicals with one unpaired electron each. It needs UV light or heating.
steps: Even split of the shared pair: one electron to each atom.
Products are two radicals.
Conditions: UV light or heat.

practice.question: Write an equation, using fish hook arrows to show electron movement, for homolytic fission of iodine, I2.
practice.answer: I–I → I• + I•, with one fish hook arrow from the bond to each iodine atom.
steps: Draw the I–I bond.
From the middle of the bond, draw one single-barbed arrow to each I atom.
Each iodine ends up with one unpaired electron: I• + I•.

practice.question: Ethane, C2H6, reacts with chlorine in sunlight. State the type of reaction and the name of its mechanism. [1]
steps: One H in ethane is replaced by Cl.
The mechanism involves radicals: SR.

practice.question: Write equations for two propagation steps and one termination step in the formation of chloroethane from ethane and chlorine. [3]
practice.answer: Propagation: C2H6 + •Cl → •C2H5 + HCl; •C2H5 + Cl2 → C2H5Cl + •Cl. Termination (any one): •C2H5 + •C2H5 → C4H10, or •C2H5 + •Cl → C2H5Cl, or •Cl + •Cl → Cl2.
steps: First propagation: Cl• takes an H from ethane, giving an ethyl radical and HCl.
Second propagation: ethyl radical takes Cl from Cl2, giving C2H5Cl and a new Cl•.
Termination: any two radicals combine into a non-radical.

practice.question: Draw or describe the structural formula of methylbenzene (toluene), C6H5CH3.
practice.answer: A benzene ring (C6H5–) with a CH3 group attached to one ring carbon.
steps: Start from the benzene ring.
Replace one ring H with a CH3 group.

practice.question: Methylbenzene is chlorinated with UV light to give chloromethylbenzene. What does the UV light do in the initiation step? [1]
practice.answer: It supplies the energy needed to break the Cl–Cl bond homolytically.
steps: Breaking a covalent bond requires energy.
UV light provides it, forming Cl• radicals.

practice.question: Write the equation for the initiation step in the chlorination of methylbenzene. [1]
steps: Initiation is homolytic fission of the halogen: Cl2 → 2Cl•.

practice.question: Write equations for two propagation steps and one termination step in the chlorination of methylbenzene, C6H5CH3, to C6H5CH2Cl. [3]
practice.answer: Propagation: C6H5CH3 + Cl• → C6H5CH2• + HCl; C6H5CH2• + Cl2 → C6H5CH2Cl + Cl•. Termination (any one): 2Cl• → Cl2, or 2C6H5CH2• → C6H5CH2CH2C6H5, or C6H5CH2• + Cl• → C6H5CH2Cl.
steps: Cl• removes an H from the CH3 group.
The resulting radical reacts with Cl2 to give the product and regenerate Cl•.
Termination: two radicals join.

practice.question: Write the overall equation for the chlorination of methylbenzene to chloromethylbenzene, using structural formulas. [3]
practice.answer: C6H5CH3 + Cl2 → C6H5CH2Cl + HCl (UV light), with the Cl replacing one H on the CH3 carbon.
steps: Reactants: methylbenzene and Cl2.
One H on the side-chain carbon is replaced by Cl.
The other products: HCl.

practice.question: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C4H9Br?
steps: Butane skeleton: 1-bromobutane and 2-bromobutane.
Branched skeleton (2-methylpropane): 1-bromo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
Total 4. (The formula was garbled in the scan; C4H9Br fits the book's answer C.)

practice.question: Compare and contrast homolytic and heterolytic fission of covalent bonds.
practice.answer: Similar: both break a covalent bond so the shared pair is no longer shared, split one species into two, and are endothermic. Different: homolytic is symmetric, one electron to each atom, giving uncharged radicals; heterolytic is asymmetric, both electrons go to one atom, giving a cation and an anion.
steps: Similarities: bond breaks, one species becomes two, energy absorbed.
Homolytic: even split, two radicals, no charges.
Heterolytic: both electrons to one fragment, giving oppositely charged ions.

practice.question: Ethane, C2H6, reacts with bromine, Br2. State the type of reaction and the conditions needed.
practice.answer: Radical substitution (SR); UV light or heat.
steps: Br replaces H on an alkane via radicals.
Radicals form only with UV light or heating.

practice.question: Write equations for the initiation, propagation and termination steps in the formation of bromoethane from ethane and bromine.
practice.answer: Initiation: Br2 → 2Br•. Propagation: CH3CH3 + Br• → •CH2CH3 + HBr; •CH2CH3 + Br2 → CH3CH2Br + Br•. Termination (any): •CH2CH3 + Br• → CH3CH2Br; 2Br• → Br2; 2•CH2CH3 → CH3CH2CH2CH3.
steps: Initiation: homolytic fission of Br2.
Propagation: Br• abstracts H, then the ethyl radical takes Br from Br2.
Termination: two radicals combine.
Put the radical dot on the atom with the unpaired electron (C or Br, not H).

worked.title: Chlorination of methane: equation and mechanism
worked.problem: Methane can be chlorinated at low temperature. (a) Write the equation for one mole of methane reacting with one mole of chlorine. (b) Outline the steps of the mechanism.

steps.hint: Replace one H of methane by Cl and note the second product.
steps.work: CH4(g) + Cl2(g) → CH3Cl(g) + HCl(g), with UV light (or sunlight) needed to start it.

steps.hint: Start the chain: split the halogen homolytically.
Let a chlorine radical attack methane.
Let the methyl radical react with Cl2 to give the product and a new radical.
End the chain by joining pairs of radicals.
Check what the termination products tell you.
steps.work: Two alkyl radicals give a larger alkane (ethane here), so a mixture of products forms. 'Outline' needs no electron arrows.
